title: Most Recent Action
scenario: Find the most recent 'action' performed by each user. Return the result table as 'user_id' and 'action'.
tableSchema: signups (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME), confirmations (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME, action VARCHAR)
hint: Use ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by user_id ordered by time_stamp DESC to pick the latest action.
correctQuery: SELECT user_id, action FROM (SELECT user_id, action, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY time_stamp DESC) as rn FROM confirmations) t WHERE rn = 1;
setupSQL: CREATE TABLE confirmations (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME, action VARCHAR); INSERT INTO confirmations VALUES (3, '2021-01-06 03:30:46', 'timeout'), (3, '2021-07-14 14:00:00', 'confirmed'), (2, '2021-01-22 00:00:00', 'confirmed');
